title: Upstart Alternatives 2026: Loan Rates and Fees Compared
h1: Upstart Alternatives 2026: Loan Rates and Fees Compared
metaDescription: Upstart alternatives compared: Prosper, Best Egg, Upgrade, Avant, OneMain Financial and Happy Money, with published loan rates, terms and fees.
intro:
Prosper, Best Egg, Upgrade, Avant, OneMain Financial and Happy Money are six Upstart alternatives for personal loans. Published Annual Percentage Rate (APR) ranges all end at 35.99%. The low end runs from 6.1% at Upstart to 11.99% at OneMain Financial. Published origination fees run from 0.99% at Best Egg to 10% at OneMain Financial.

At The Modern Wallet, we compare published borrowing fees and rate schedules so borrowers can calculate net proceeds and loan costs before submitting an application. The subject is [Upstart](https://www.upstart.com/personal-loans), which offers fixed-rate personal loans from $1,000 to $75,000 with three-year or five-year terms. Its homepage also lists a Cash Line from $50 to $500 and short-term relief loans from $200 to $2,500. It also lists a Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) through Upstart Home Lending.

Selecting a personal loan depends on borrowing amounts, origination fee deductions, repayment term options and qualifying criteria. For broader context on evaluating lending offers, explore the [best personal loans guidance in our personal loan review guide](/guides/how-to-read-a-personal-loan-review/) and see if an unsecured option fits compared to secured borrowing in our [HELOC vs personal loan](/compare/heloc-vs-personal-loan/) breakdown. If you are weighing fixed installment structures, review our [home equity loan vs personal loan](/compare/home-equity-loan-vs-personal-loan/) analysis, or consult our [comparison hub](/compare/) for additional side-by-side lending tables.

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose an Upstart Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Three loan sizes show how a published origination fee changes the cash a borrower receives. The figures below are arithmetic on published percentages, rounded to the nearest dollar. They are not a quote or an offer. The Upstart line uses the 8.31% fee from Upstart's own example, since Upstart publishes no fee range.

- Best Egg low end, 0.99% (terms under four years): $50 on $5,000 (net $4,950); $99 on $10,000 (net $9,901); $248 on $25,000 (net $24,752)
- Prosper low end, 1%: $50 on $5,000 (net $4,950); $100 on $10,000 (net $9,900); $250 on $25,000 (net $24,750)
- Upgrade low end, 1.85%: $93 on $5,000 (net $4,907); $185 on $10,000 (net $9,815); $463 on $25,000 (net $24,537)
- Happy Money calculator assumption, 3%: $150 on $5,000 (net $4,850); $300 on $10,000 (net $9,700); $750 on $25,000 (net $24,250)
- Upstart published example, 8.31%: $416 on $5,000 (net $4,584); $831 on $10,000 (net $9,169); $2,078 on $25,000 (net $22,922)
- Prosper, Best Egg, Upgrade and Avant high end, 9.99%: $500 on $5,000 (net $4,500); $999 on $10,000 (net $9,001); $2,498 on $25,000 (net $22,502)
- OneMain Financial high end, 10%: $500 on $5,000 (net $4,500); $1,000 on $10,000 (net $9,000); $2,500 on $25,000 (net $22,500)

The gap between Prosper's 1% and 9.99% ends is $450 on $5,000, $899 on $10,000 and $2,248 on $25,000. The fee a lender assigns matters as much as the headline APR floor.

Break-even counterexample: Upstart says an origination fee applies only if applicable. With no fee, net proceeds on $10,000 are $10,000, which is $831 above the 8.31% example. With the 8.31% example fee, Upstart's $9,169 trails Upgrade's minimum-fee proceeds of $9,815 by $646. Best Egg states that its origination fee on terms of four years or longer is at least 4.99%, so its 0.99% line applies to shorter terms only.

Four published criteria frame the rest of the choice:

- Loan size: Upstart lists $1,000 to $75,000, and minimums vary by state (Georgia $3,100, Hawaii $1,500, Massachusetts $7,000). Prosper, Best Egg, Upgrade and Happy Money cap at $50,000. Avant and OneMain Financial cap at $35,000. Minimums are $1,000 at Upgrade, $1,500 at OneMain Financial, $2,000 at Prosper, Best Egg and Avant, and $5,000 at Happy Money. Avant's minimums also vary by state.
- Fee schedule: Prosper lists 1% to 9.99%, Best Egg 0.99% to 9.99%, Upgrade 1.85% to 9.99% and Avant up to 9.99% as an administration fee. OneMain Financial lists a flat $25 to $500 or 1% to 10%, depending on state and loan.
- Terms: Upstart offers three or five years. Upgrade spans 24 to 84 months, Prosper two to six years, and Avant, OneMain Financial and Happy Money 24 to 60 months.
- Credit check: Upstart, Prosper, Best Egg, Upgrade and Avant each state that checking a rate uses a soft inquiry with no effect on the credit score.

alternatives.heading: Prosper Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Prosper offers fixed-rate personal loans from $2,000 to $50,000 with repayment terms from two to six years. Its published APR ranges from 8.99% to 35.99%. Prosper charges an origination fee of 1% to 9.99%, which is a published fee. Additional fees listed on its website include a check payment fee, late payment fee and insufficient funds fee. Prosper states that checking your rate does not affect your credit score, and there is never a prepayment penalty.

Prosper fits borrowers seeking flexible repayment durations between two and six years for amounts up to $50,000.

Versus Upstart, Prosper caps borrowing at $50,000, whereas Upstart offers loans up to $75,000. Upstart's published APR range starts lower at 6.1%, compared to Prosper's minimum rate of 8.99%. However, Prosper publishes its complete origination fee range of 1% to 9.99%, while Upstart states that origination fees apply only if applicable without publishing a minimum or maximum range.

Worked cost example: On a $10,000 loan, Prosper's published representative example illustrates a three-year term at a 17.29% interest rate with an 8.99% origination fee. That 8.99% fee equals $899, leaving the borrower with $9,101 in net loan proceeds. At Prosper's lowest fee tier of 1%, the origination fee is $100, leaving $9,900. By comparison, Upstart's published representative example on a $10,000 loan shows an 8.31% origination fee ($831), delivering $9,169 to the borrower, which is $68 more in net proceeds than Prosper's 8.99% example. Readers who want more on this lender can read our guide on [is Prosper a good personal loan lender](/guides/is-prosper-a-good-personal-loan-lender/).

alternatives.heading: Best Egg Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Best Egg provides fixed-rate personal loans from $2,000 to $50,000 with illustrated terms of 36 and 60 months. Best Egg publishes an APR range from 6.99% to 35.99%. The APR reflects an origination fee ranging from 0.99% to 9.99%, which is deducted directly from loan proceeds. Best Egg states that the origination fee on terms of four years or longer is at least 4.99%. Best Egg charges no prepayment fees or penalties, and states that checking your rate does not impact your credit score.

Best Egg fits borrowers who want an origination fee starting at 0.99% on shorter terms.

Versus Upstart, Best Egg limits borrowing to $50,000, leaving borrowers needing $50,001 to $75,000 unserved. Best Egg's lowest published APR is 6.99%, which sits 0.89 percentage points above Upstart's 6.1% entry rate. However, Best Egg's 0.99% minimum origination fee is the lowest published percentage floor among the lenders on this page.

Worked cost example: On a $10,000 loan, an applicant qualifying for Best Egg's 0.99% origination fee pays $99, receiving $9,901 in net cash. At Best Egg's upper fee limit of 9.99%, the deduction is $999, resulting in $9,001 in net proceeds. On a $25,000 loan, a 0.99% fee equals $247.50 (rounded to $248), delivering $24,752, while a 9.99% fee deducts $2,497.50 (rounded to $2,498), delivering $22,502. Under Upstart's representative example of 8.31%, the fee on $25,000 is $2,077.50 (rounded to $2,078), delivering $22,922.

alternatives.heading: Upgrade Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Upgrade offers personal loans from $1,000 to $50,000 with repayment terms from 24 to 84 months. Its published APR spans from 7.74% to 35.99%. Upgrade charges an origination fee of 1.85% to 9.99%, which is deducted from proceeds before disbursement. Upgrade specifies that receiving its lowest rates requires enrolling in Autopay and using loan funds to pay off a portion of existing debt directly. Checking your rate involves a soft inquiry, and Upgrade charges no prepayment fees.

Upgrade fits borrowers who want repayment terms extending up to 84 months or who want funds sent directly to existing creditors for debt consolidation.

Versus Upstart, Upgrade limits borrowing to $50,000, whereas Upstart offers up to $75,000. Upstart also publishes a lower APR floor at 6.1% compared to Upgrade's 7.74%. Conversely, Upgrade provides terms up to 84 months (seven years), while Upstart restricts options to 36 or 60 months.

Worked cost example: On a $10,000 loan, Upgrade's published example illustrates a 36-month term with a 5% origination fee ($500), delivering $9,500 in net proceeds. If a borrower receives Upgrade's lowest fee of 1.85%, the deduction is $185, leaving $9,815. At Upgrade's maximum 9.99% fee, the deduction is $999, leaving $9,001. Compared with Upstart's representative example deducting $831 (8.31%) on $10,000, Upgrade's 5% example provides $331 more in cash proceeds.

alternatives.heading: Avant Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Avant issues personal loans ranging from $2,000 to $35,000 with repayment terms of 24 to 60 months. Its published APR runs from 9.95% to 35.99%. Avant charges an administration fee of up to 9.99%, which reduces the amount financed. Avant states that checking loan options does not impact your credit score.

Avant fits borrowers who need loan amounts up to $35,000 and select terms between two and five years.

Versus Upstart, Avant sets a much lower borrowing ceiling of $35,000 compared to Upstart's $75,000 cap. Upstart also starts loans at $1,000, whereas Avant sets a $2,000 minimum. Upstart publishes an APR starting at 6.1%, which is 3.85 percentage points lower than Avant's 9.95% minimum APR. Avant refers to its upfront charge as an administration fee rather than an origination fee.

Worked cost example: On Avant's published website example, a borrower obtains a $5,700 loan with a 9.99% administration fee, resulting in $5,130.57 financed, repaid over 36 monthly payments of $217.66 at a 29.95% APR. The 9.99% fee equals $569.43. On a standard $5,000 loan at Avant's maximum 9.99% administration fee, the charge is $499.50 (rounded to $500), yielding $4,500 in net cash. Under Upstart's representative example rate of 8.31%, the fee on $5,000 is $415.50 (rounded to $416), delivering $4,584 in proceeds.

alternatives.heading: OneMain Financial Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
OneMain Financial provides personal loans from $1,500 to $35,000 with fixed repayment terms of 24 to 60 months. Its published APR ranges from 11.99% to 35.99%. OneMain Financial structures its origination fee based on state law and loan size, charging either a flat fee from $25 to $500 or a percentage from 1% to 10%. Late payment fees may also apply.

OneMain Financial fits borrowers who qualify for a flat dollar origination fee structure rather than a percentage-based deduction.

Versus Upstart, OneMain Financial publishes a maximum loan limit of $35,000, which is $40,000 lower than Upstart's $75,000 maximum. Upstart's APR floor of 6.1% is 5.89 percentage points below OneMain Financial's 11.99% starting rate. However, for borrowers taking larger loans in jurisdictions where OneMain Financial charges a flat dollar fee, the total fee can be lower than a high percentage deduction.

Worked cost example: On a $10,000 loan, an origination fee charged as a flat $500 deduction leaves $9,500 in proceeds. If OneMain Financial applies a 10% percentage fee, the deduction is $1,000, delivering $9,000. If the fee is 1%, the deduction is $100, delivering $9,900. On a $25,000 loan, a flat fee of $500 represents an effective charge of only 2% ($500 divided by $25,000), leaving $24,500 in proceeds, whereas a 10% fee takes $2,500, leaving $22,500. Under Upstart's published representative example of 8.31%, the fee on $25,000 is $2,077.50 (rounded to $2,078), delivering $22,922.

alternatives.heading: Happy Money Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Happy Money offers personal loans from $5,000 to $50,000 designed specifically for paying off credit card balances. It publishes fixed APRs starting as low as 8.95% for the life of the loan, with terms of 24, 36, 48 or 60 months. Happy Money's online calculator assumes an origination fee of 3%, as published in its calculator.

Happy Money fits borrowers who want to consolidate credit card debt with loans of $5,000 or more.

Versus Upstart, Happy Money enforces a higher minimum borrowing requirement of $5,000, while Upstart allows loans starting at $1,000. Upstart also allows loans up to $75,000, exceeding Happy Money's $50,000 cap. Upstart's APR range starts at 6.1%, compared to Happy Money's 8.95% minimum. Happy Money describes its loan as built for clearing high-interest credit card balances.

Worked cost example: On a $10,000 loan, assuming Happy Money's 3% calculator origination fee, the fee deduction is $300, delivering $9,700 in proceeds. On a $25,000 loan, a 3% fee equals $750, leaving $24,250 in proceeds. By comparison, Upstart's representative example of an 8.31% fee deducts $831 on $10,000 (delivering $9,169) and $2,077.50 (rounded to $2,078) on $25,000 (delivering $22,922). On a $10,000 loan, Happy Money's 3% assumed fee delivers $531 more in net cash than Upstart's 8.31% representative example.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Personal loan comparisons do not fit every borrowing situation. This page is not suitable for several categories of consumers:

- Borrowers needing loans over $75,000: Upstart tops out at $75,000, while Prosper, Best Egg, Upgrade and Happy Money cap loans at $50,000, and Avant and OneMain Financial stop at $35,000. 
- Borrowers who want a guaranteed APR: every rate on this page is a published range and no lender has promised it to any reader. Actual APRs vary by applicant and state of residence.
- Borrowers who need micro-loans under $1,000: Upstart and Upgrade set their minimum loan amounts at $1,000, with state variations at Upstart, while other lenders require $1,500, $2,000 or $5,000. Upstart offers a separate Cash Line from $50 to $500, but personal loans on this page do not serve sub-$1,000 borrowing.
- Borrowers who want zero-fee guarantees: while Upstart notes that origination fees apply if applicable, every alternative here publishes or assumes an origination or administration fee that reduces proceeds.

If you own substantial home equity, reviewing secured options in our [home equity loan vs personal loan](/compare/home-equity-loan-vs-personal-loan/) analysis can provide alternative rate structures.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer
alternatives.body:
This comparison reflects published rates, fees and terms as of November 27, 2026. These changes would shift it:

- Upstart publishing an origination fee range would allow exact comparison with Prosper and Best Egg.
- A $75,000 cap at another lender would end Upstart's lead on loan size.
- A change in Upstart's 6.1% APR floor would narrow or widen the gap to Best Egg at 6.99% and Upgrade at 7.74%.
- OneMain Financial dropping its flat $25 to $500 fee would remove its dollar-fee option.
- Happy Money lowering its $5,000 minimum would put it in reach of smaller balances.
- A change to the 35.99% APR ceiling at any lender would alter every high-end cost.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Upstart Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Upstart remains the better fit for borrowers who require loan amounts exceeding $50,000 up to $75,000, as all six alternatives on this page cap unsecured personal loans at $35,000 or $50,000. Upstart also publishes the lowest starting APR of the group, with APRs beginning at 6.1% for the most qualified applicants, though rates vary by state.

Upstart also fits borrowers who want a rate check that takes about 5 minutes and does not affect their credit score (soft inquiry). Personal loans carry fixed rates with three-year or five-year terms (36 or 60 months) and have no prepayment penalties, allowing borrowers to pay off the principal balance early without incurring additional charges. Upstart says an origination fee applies only if applicable. With no fee, net proceeds on a $10,000 loan are $10,000. That is more than any alternative charging a published minimum fee.

Upstart also lists adjacent products on its homepage. Cash Line offers $50 to $500 if approved. Short-term relief loans run $200 to $2,500 over 3 to 18 months, with an example at 35.95% APR. A home equity line of credit from Upstart Home Lending runs $26,000 to $250,000, with initial advance rates as low as 6.52% APR.

verdict:
Upstart lists loans up to $75,000 with APRs starting at 6.1%. The alternatives cap loans at $35,000 or $50,000. Best Egg publishes the lowest fee floor at 0.99%, and Upgrade offers terms up to 84 months. Prosper offers two to six years. Happy Money targets credit card debt with an assumed 3% fee. Avant serves loans up to $35,000, and OneMain Financial lists flat-dollar fee options.

Each lender's own rate check shows the fee and APR it would assign an applicant. The [comparison hub](/compare/) lists other lending tables.

faqs.question: What should I use instead of Upstart for a personal loan?
faqs.answer: Prosper, Best Egg, Upgrade, Avant, OneMain Financial and Happy Money are six Upstart alternatives. Best Egg offers origination fees starting at 0.99%, Upgrade provides terms up to 84 months, and Prosper offers terms from two to six years. Upstart is the only lender among them offering loans up to $75,000.

faqs.question: Which Upstart alternative has the lowest origination fee?
faqs.answer: Best Egg publishes the lowest minimum origination fee, starting at 0.99% of the loan amount. Prosper starts at 1%, Upgrade starts at 1.85%, and OneMain Financial starts at 1% or a flat $25. Upstart states an origination fee applies if applicable but does not publish a percentage range.

faqs.question: Can checking rates on Upstart alternatives affect your credit score?
faqs.answer: No. Upstart, Prosper, Best Egg, Upgrade and Avant all state that checking your rate or loan options uses a soft inquiry that does not affect your credit score.

faqs.question: Do Upstart alternatives charge prepayment penalties?
faqs.answer: Upstart, Prosper, Best Egg and Upgrade all state on their websites that they charge no prepayment fees or penalties if you pay off your loan early.

faqs.question: Which lender offers the largest personal loan among these alternatives?
faqs.answer: Upstart offers the largest maximum personal loan, allowing qualified applicants to borrow up to $75,000. Prosper, Best Egg, Upgrade and Happy Money cap their personal loans at $50,000, while Avant and OneMain Financial cap borrowing at $35,000.
